jobs.title: Manager Sales Strategy & Planning
jobs.description:
Job Details:
Summary:

The SS&P Manager is a key member of the Foodservice Prepared team, supporting the K–12 and Distribution channels. This role handles day-to-day execution and support, and helps deliver against annual financial and volume targets for Tyson Foodservice Prepared categories. The Manager works alongside the Senior Managers who set growth strategy 12+ months out, and turns that strategy into reliable results for customers and the field.

This position is a critical link between field sales, supply chain, demand planning, and business unit teams. The Manager is the go-to resource for customer and field questions that need more than the tools and information on hand, and turns insights into actions that improve execution in market. The role emphasizes performance analytics, distribution effectiveness, and channel-specific dynamics, including distributor network performance.

The SS&P Manager works in a highly cross-functional environment and plays a central role in aligning strategy with execution, so the sales organization can win with customers and operators. The ideal candidate shows strong ownership, analytical capability, and a proactive mindset, and can quickly synthesize information into clear recommendations.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities
- Performance & Insights: Analyze category and product performance. Deliver actionable insights that identify growth opportunities and risks.
- Strategy & Planning: Support development and execution of K–12 and Distribution channel strategies aligned to business objectives.
- Sales Support: Partner with field sales to translate strategy into clear priorities, tools, and actions that drive in-market execution.
- Customer Resolution: Serve as the go-to resource for customer and field questions and issues that go beyond available tools and resources, driving each to resolution.
- Distribution & Execution: Monitor distributor performance, product distribution, and operator penetration. Identify and close execution gaps.
- Demand & Readiness: Manage day-to-day demand, forecast, inventory, and CID/load-in readiness, using Customer Insights data.
- Forecasting & S&OP: Provide input to demand forecasts and actively participate in S&OP to align on trends, risks, and opportunities.
- Promotions: Develop short-term promotional growth opportunities, including Truck Load, and support promo execution.
- Product Impact Management: Monitor product impacts (fill rate, capacity, SKU) and troubleshoot the resulting customer service issues. Recommend support solutions for customers, align get-well dates with the business unit, and communicate them to the field.
- Business Enablement & Communications: Develop and maintain customer- and channel-facing materials (brand material, sell sheets, attribute file) and field communications that support sales execution across K–12 and Distribution.
- Cross-Functional Collaboration: Serve as the key liaison across sales, supply chain, demand planning, and business teams to ensure alignment and results.
- Request Management: Manage incoming field and customer requests.
- Model behaviors that support Tyson Foods' behaviors and leadership principles.

Requirements:

Education:
- Bachelor's Degree required

Experience:
- Minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in customer trade marketing, sales, marketing, sales analytics, revenue management or category management.
- Demonstrated financial acumen, with joint growth planning experience a plus
- Demonstrated ability to partner with and influence cross-functional team members

Communication Skills:
- Excellent organizational and communication skills;
- Strong influencing and negotiating skills.
- Strong ability to articulate complex information in a concise manner and with proper context

Computer Skills:
- Intermediate-Advanced level for MS Excel, Word, PowerPoint & Teams;
- Prior experience with Tyson CRM preferred

Special Skills:
- Excellent planning and project management skills
- Syndicated Data experience
- Strong Excel and data manipulation skills
- Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills
- Business acumen and ownership

Direct Reports: 0
Travel: Some travel is required, up to 10% of time

jobs.location: Green Forest Plant - Green Forest, Arkansas
jobs.description:
Job Details:
Continuous Improvement Leader
Summary
The Continuous Improvement (CI) Leader is responsible for driving and sustaining a culture of continuous improvement throughout the facility. This role serves as the subject matter expert for Continuous Improvement initiatives, providing training, coaching, and leadership to Production Team Members, Engineers, and Functional Leaders. The CI Leader partners with all levels of the organization to implement Lean principles, lead change management efforts, and improve operational performance.
This position focuses on enhancing safety, food safety, quality, delivery performance, inventory management, cost reduction, and overall process efficiency. The CI Leader facilitates improvement projects, develops operational excellence strategies, and ensures measurable results that support business objectives.
Key Responsibilities
- Lead and facilitate Kaizen events and Rapid Improvement Processes (RIPs).
- Identify, analyze, and track improvement opportunities through data collection and performance metrics.
- Promote compliance with safety, environmental, food safety, and quality standards.
- Demonstrate expertise in Lean Manufacturing principles and Continuous Improvement methodologies.
- Develop and implement strategies that improve productivity, efficiency, and process effectiveness.
- Train and coach employees at all levels on problem-solving tools and methodologies, including: - Process Mapping
- Standardized Work
- Lean Manufacturing
- Six Sigma
- Time and Cost Management

- Lead Continuous Improvement projects focused on process optimization, cost reduction, and performance improvement.
- Maintain project schedules, progress reports, and documentation demonstrating measurable operational improvements.
- Partner with plant leadership to analyze staffing, labor utilization, capacity, and operational performance.
- Calculate and validate cost savings and improvement opportunities.
- Collaborate with the Plant Controller to document financial results and project savings.
- Monitor and report the status of all CI initiatives to plant leadership.
- Validate and confirm production standards and process expectations.
- Assist in monitoring equipment effectiveness (OEE) and partner with Maintenance to identify TPM, repair, and reliability opportunities.
- Develop and maintain value stream maps for key processes and product families.
- Support additional Continuous Improvement initiatives as assigned by the Senior Manager of Continuous Improvement.

Qualifications
Education
- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, or a related field preferred.
- Equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered.

Experience
- Five or more years of demonstrated Continuous Improvement experience; or
- Five or more years of leadership experience in a Lean manufacturing environment.
- Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification, or progress toward certification, preferred.

Communication Skills
- Ability to effectively communicate and influence individuals at all levels of the organization.
- Strong coaching, mentoring, and facilitation skills.

Travel
- Minimal travel required (four or fewer trips per year).

Technical and Leadership Skills
- Strong business acumen and analytical skills.
- Extensive knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, 5S, Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping, and other Continuous Improvement methodologies.
- Strong process management and project leadership experience.
- Ability to lead change, drive accountability, and deliver measurable operational results.
- Proven ability to influence cross-functional teams and foster a culture of continuous improvement.

jobs.title: Senior Manager Business Intelligence - Innovation
jobs.description:
Job Details:
Enterprise Analytics & Business Intelligence at Tyson Foods is a discipline closely linked to marketing and consumer-driven business decisions, grounded in deeply understanding business drivers, competitive intelligence, foresight, innovation sizing, category and business forecasting, investment ROIs, and pricing dynamics.
As Senior Manager, Innovation Analytics, you will lead the analytics agenda across the full innovation lifecycle, serving as the strategic bridge between data and decision-making. This role owns four interconnected pillars of the Innovation Analytics structure — Strategy, Forecasting, Story Telling, and In-Market Tracking — transforming complex internal and syndicated data into compelling narratives and forward-looking forecasts that enable successful product launches at Tyson Foods.
You will synthesize multiple data sources (e.g., Nielsen, Circana/IRI, Luminate, 84.51°, Mintel, Datassential, and others) to analyze and interpret the business, reporting into the Director of Innovation Analytics. This individual will maintain a critical consulting and advisory role with senior management across the organization, driving best practices in analytics while building capabilities and influence major product decisions. A proven record of leadership, strategic thinking, and persuasive communication is essential.

Responsibilities
Innovation Strategy & Communication Funnel
- Shape the enterprise innovation strategy by informing how much innovation is needed per year, total platforms needed, total line extensions vs. core, distribution expectations, SKU rationalization, and new categories and adjacencies.

- Drive alignment between Innovation and Business Units based on Category Development needs, providing objective review of possibilities to drive strategic initiatives.

- Be a leader in driving business decisions based on market data, establishing key drivers and providing actionable “call to action” recommendations for growth.

- Drive a culture of foresight to anticipate future business momentum, both short and long term; be predictive in how business and market share will be impacted in the future.

Forecasting & Resource Development
- Coordinate with the Innovation team on Size of Prize for initial project proposals, ensuring rigorous, objective sizing of new opportunities.

- Develop deep, data-driven customer-level forecasts through internally developed tools, including volumetric, market share, distribution, and velocity forecasting for innovation estimates.

- Ensure Business Unit and Sales alignment on short-term and long-range projections for innovation projects.

Story Telling & Innovation Enablement
- Build best-in-class sales stories: gather insights from stakeholders and syndicated data sources, identify story gaps, and facilitate key contributors to close needed data points.

- Synthesize data into best-in-class communication — insight-driven sales tools, sell-in decks, and marketing narratives — that informs and empowers sales team members and supports innovation commercialization.

- Frame data to highlight opportunity, risk, and recommended action with clarity and confidence, maintaining a strong narrative flow from insight to action.

- Develop future outlooks, supporting brand strategy development that leads to cohesive stories.

In-Market Tracking & Performance
- Monitor and track key KPIs versus expected forecast and goals across the innovation portfolio.

- Provide clear communication to Business Units and Sales on drivers of success or gaps in performance.

- Deep dive issues and provide detailed, actionable recommendations to resolve performance gaps.

- Establish KPIs and new capabilities as best practice for measuring the impact of new product development, distribution, velocities, and other activations for innovation products.

- Lead analytics throughout the complete product lifecycle, including brand strategy, communication strategy, innovation, product and packaging, in-market execution, and assessment.

Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration
- Partner with Innovation Marketing, Brand, Sales, Consumer Insights, Category, and Business Unit stakeholders to ensure cohesive storytelling and shared understanding of innovation strategies.

- Lead alignment meetings to streamline communication around key metrics and performance drivers related to new product launches.

- Be a leader in solving complex business challenges through cross-functional collaboration to address key business questions.

- Drive best practices in analytics across the organization, building capabilities, developing talent, and building advocacy for analytics.

- Represent Tyson's Business Intelligence team in professional organizations and meetings.

Qualifications
Education

Job Details:
Summary
The Marketing Manager supports brand strategy execution for the identified brand portfolio, translating the Senior Manager's strategic direction into day-to-day marketing plans, campaigns, and cross-functional deliverables. The core mandate is executional excellence: bringing the brand strategy to life across touchpoints, managing the details that make campaigns and launches successful, and building the analytical and operational foundation that lets the Senior Manager focus on strategy. This is a strong development role for someone building toward broader brand ownership.

This position will sit full time onsite at our World Headquarters in Springdale, Arkansas.

Key Responsibilities
- Brand Positioning & Strategy: In partnership with the Sr. Manager, own and evolve the brand strategy for the brand portfolio, including brand purpose, positioning, target consumer definition, and competitive differentiation, in partnership with the business unit GM and team. Ensure brand guidelines are understood and consistently applied across teams and agency partners.
- Consumer & Insights: Synthesize as well as recommend quantitative and qualitative consumer data (segmentation, usage & attitude studies, purchase behavior, social listening) to identify unmet needs and emerging trends; translate findings into clear, actionable insights that inform brand positioning, innovation priorities, and go-to-market strategy; partner with consumer insights teams to design and prioritize research that closes critical knowledge gaps.
- Campaign & Program Execution: Manage the day-to-day execution of marketing campaigns and brand initiatives — timelines, deliverables, approvals, and stakeholder coordination — ensuring on-time, on-brief, on-budget delivery.
- Brand Performance Tracking: Track brand health metrics, market share, and campaign performance against KPIs; prepare regular performance reports and highlight areas needing attention.
- Cross-Functional Leadership: Serve as the strategic connective tissue across creative, media, shopper marketing, social, and digital experience to ensure a consistent, on-brand experience across all consumer touchpoints; partner with media agency partners to shape media strategy — channel mix, audience targeting, and investment allocation — ensuring plans align with brand positioning and growth priorities; manage agency relationships (creative, media, and specialist partners) to drive high-quality output, accountability to brief, and efficient use of budget.

jobs.description:
Job Details:
Role Summary

The Senior Manager Procurement – Technology is responsible for leading sourcing and contracting activities across the Technology portfolio, delivering strong commercial outcomes while enabling business and IT priorities. This role focuses on execution excellence, disciplined contracting, and trusted stakeholder partnership across enterprise technology needs, including Corporate functions and Supply Chain.
Reporting to the Associate Director Procurement – Technology, this role serves as a primary procurement partner to Technology and business leaders and is accountable for applying consistent sourcing and contracting practices across:
- Software licensing (SaaS, on‑prem, subscription, consumption‑based)

- Cloud services and hosting

- Telecom and network services

- Hardware and infrastructure

- Technology professional services

The role may include people management responsibilities, depending on portfolio, scope, and future team structure.

Key Responsibilities
Technology Sourcing & Contracting Execution
- Lead end‑to‑end sourcing and contracting activities for assigned Technology categories.

- Execute sourcing events, negotiations, and renewals to meet aggressive timelines while maintaining consistent commercial and contractual standards.

- Negotiate and redline commercial terms, including pricing models, service levels, renewal protections, and contractual risk provisions.

- Ensure agreements comply with company policies, governance standards, and regulatory requirements.

- Apply repeatable sourcing and contracting approaches across the Technology vertical that aligns with how other Corporate Services categories operate.

- Partner closely with Legal and Risk teams to drive timely and high‑quality contract outcomes.

Stakeholder Partnership
- Act as a primary procurement partner to Technology stakeholders, helping teams engage procurement early and navigate sourcing and contracting efficiently.

- Balance need for speed and flexibility with appropriate governance and risk management.

- Serve as a point of escalation for complex, high‑risk, or time‑sensitive sourcing and contracting matters.

Process Consistency & Governance
- Reinforce consistent procurement processes across Technology that align with broader Corporate Services standards.

- Ensure sourcing documentation, approvals, and contracting requirements are followed across all Technology activity.

- Support visibility into upcoming renewals and sourcing demand to reduce last‑minute escalations and execution risk.

- Contribute to continuous improvement of Technology workflows and stakeholder experience.

People Leadership & Team Support
- Provide guidance and support for Category Managers executing Technology sourcing activity.

- Coach team members on setting and executing negotiation strategies, commercial term redlining, and stakeholder engagement as needed.

- Help prioritize work and remove blockers during peak workload periods.

Qualifications & Experience
- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience

- Strong understanding of technology sourcing models, including software licensing, cloud, telecom, and professional services.

- 7+ years of Procurement, Strategic Sourcing, or Category Management experience, with direct experience supporting Technology spend.

- Demonstrated ability to review, negotiate, and redline commercial contract terms in a fast‑paced environment.

- Experience with Source‑to‑Pay and Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) tools preferred

- Strong proficiency in analytical tools (spreadsheets, cost models, savings tracking)

- Ability to apply consistent procurement processes across a diverse Technology portfolio

- Effective communicator able to engage stakeholders at multiple levels.

- Proven negotiation and contract management experience with complex service‑based suppliers.

- Proven experience partnering cross‑functionally
